name: Arsia Mons south-west flank
blurb: The south-west flank of Arsia Mons, 15 km up: dark lava plains broken by collapse pits and the roofs of lava tubes, some fallen in to leave open skylights into the dark.

projection.name: Equirectangular, Mars 2000 sphere, true scale at -10.85 deg (latTs = lat0), centred on 239.05 E
projection.note: x = R cos(lat_ts) (lon - lon_0), y = R lat (radians): projected metres are true metres at the site's latitude; cos_lat0 (the world scale factor) is therefore 1

grid.convention: sample (i,j) of a level is centred at x0+(i+0.5)*mpp, y0-(j+0.5)*mpp; tile (tx,ty) holds samples tx*tile.. and ty*tile..
grid.world: game X = east metres from the site centre = x - x_centre; game Z = south metres = y_centre - y; game Y = height_m - height.ref

height.encoding: height_m = offset + (R*256 + G) * scale; B = provenance

provenance_byte.255: Mars Express HRSC DTM h0263_0000 (DA4, heights above the areoid), 100 m (100 m posts)
provenance_byte.64: Mars MGS MOLA - MEX HRSC Blended DEM Global 200 m, v2 (USGS Astrogeology) (200 m posts)
provenance_byte.0: no data (filled from the nearest valid sample)

255.text: Mars Express HRSC DTM h0263_0000 (DA4, heights above the areoid), 100 m

64.text: Mars MGS MOLA - MEX HRSC Blended DEM Global 200 m, v2 (USGS Astrogeology)

labels.0: no data (filled from the nearest valid sample)

levelling.method: each layer stretched to 8 bits once per site (0.5 / 99.5 percentiles of the first layer; later layers matched to it in mean and spread where they overlap), then feathered in priority order

imagery.colour: Viking MDIM 2.1 colour (232 m), resampled to 80 m: modulates the hue of the ground; the brightness comes from the imagery

colour_tex.what: Viking MDIM 2.1 colour (232 m), resampled to 80 m: modulates the hue of the ground; the brightness comes from the imagery

levels.what: Mars Express HRSC DTM h0263_0000 (100 m) feathered over Mars MGS MOLA - MEX HRSC Blended DEM Global 200 m, v2 (200 m), cubic-resampled to 16 m
the 16 m level upsampled to 4 m with a cubic B-spline: interpolation, nothing finer than the source posts
Mars MRO CTX equirectangular mosaic MC-17, 6 m (6 m), resampled to 5 m

hrsc_dtm.composition: HRSC multi-line stereo, level 4 (MEX-M-HRSC-5-REFDR-DTM-V1.0), areoid heights

blend.title: Mars MGS MOLA - MEX HRSC Blended DEM Global 200 m, v2 (USGS Astrogeology)
blend.composition: HRSC stereo DTMs (Mars Express) where they exist, MOLA altimetry (463 m) elsewhere, blended at 200 m; heights above the MOLA areoid
blend.licence: Public domain (USGS Astrogeology / NASA); credit the producers. Cite Fergason, Hare and Laura 2018, HRSC and MOLA Blended Digital Elevation Model at 200 m v2, USGS Astrogeology. HRSC component: ESA/DLR/FU Berlin.

ctx.title: Mars MRO CTX equirectangular mosaic MC-17, 6 m (Robbins et al., USGS Astrogeology)
ctx.composition: Context Camera (MRO CTX) images, photometrically normalised and mosaicked; 16-bit greyscale
ctx.licence: Public domain (USGS Astrogeology / NASA); credit the producers. CTX: NASA / JPL / Malin Space Science Systems. Cite Robbins et al. 2023, CTX mosaics of Mars' equatorial quadrangles (USGS Astrogeology).

colour.title: Mars Viking MDIM 2.1 colorized global mosaic, 232 m (USGS Astrogeology)
colour.composition: Viking Orbiter images (MDIM 2.1) coloured from Viking colour observations; used here only as a low-resolution colour tint
colour.licence: Public domain (USGS Astrogeology / NASA); credit the producers. Cite USGS Astrogeology, Viking MDIM 2.1 colorized mosaic (NASA / JPL / USGS).

style.name: basaltic lava flows and collapse pits

tint.from: hue of the darkest, middle and brightest fifths of the Viking MDIM 2.1 colour mosaic over the site (dark and bright pulled halfway to the middle; a hue that is not red > green > blue falls back to the game's own); brightness kept from the game's default ramp

pois.name: Landing
pois.note: Smooth lava plain on the flank, about 15.4 km above the datum. The pits to the east and west are real collapse features, mapped by CTX and resolved, coarsely, by HRSC.
pois.source: Story location (fictional), placed on the real terrain model

pois.name: Relay line end
pois.note: Where the surface relay line from the landing ends: from here the radio link to the cave runs on the line laid down the collapse ramp.
pois.source: Story location (fictional), placed on the real terrain model

pois.name: Skylight A
pois.note: A sheer-walled hole about 100 m across and 90 m deep where a lava-tube roof has fallen in. Candidates like it were found on Arsia's flanks in THEMIS and HiRISE images (Cushing et al. 2007); this one is generated.
pois.source: Story location (fictional), placed on the real terrain model

pois.name: Outpost Arsia airlock (the cave entrance)
pois.note: At the foot of the talus ramp inside a collapse pit, where the tube opens sideways: the airlock of Outpost Arsia. The cave beyond is its own scene; this is its door on the surface terrain.
pois.source: Story location (fictional), placed on the real terrain model

notes: The skylights, the collapse ramp and the small pit chains are generated features (detailstyle.js); the kilometre-scale pits and troughs are real, in the CTX imagery and (at 100 m) the HRSC terrain.
The ground is tinted darker than Arsia's dust-mantled albedo suggests (style tint lum_scale 0.62), for the lava-plain look the story asks for: the hue is still MDIM's.
quality: HRSC stereo 100 m and MOLA-HRSC 200 m terrain; CTX 6 m imagery
